Apple___Apple_scab.about: Apple scab is a widespread fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis. It primarily affects leaves, fruits, and young shoots. The disease thrives in cool, moist environments and spreads through airborne spores. If left unmanaged, it can significantly reduce fruit quality and yield, making it one of the most economically important diseases in apple cultivation.
symptoms: Olive-green to dark brown velvety spots on leaves
Scabby, rough lesions on fruit surface
Leaf distortion and premature leaf drop
Reduced fruit size and deformities
treatment: Apply protective fungicides such as captan, mancozeb, or myclobutanil at early growth stages
Remove and destroy infected leaves and fruits to reduce spore spread
Prune trees to improve airflow and reduce humidity
prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation to minimize leaf wetness
Maintain orchard sanitation by removing fallen debris

Apple___Black_rot.about: Black rot is a fungal disease caused by Botryosphaeria obtusa. It affects fruits, leaves, and bark, leading to fruit rot and branch cankers. The disease is favored by warm and humid conditions and can persist in dead plant material, making orchard sanitation critical.
symptoms: Dark circular lesions on fruit with concentric rings
Purple-bordered leaf spots
Cankers on branches with cracked bark
Fruit shriveling into mummified forms
treatment: Prune and destroy infected branches and mummified fruits
Maintain tree vigor with proper nutrition
prevention: Regularly remove dead wood and debris

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.about: Cedar apple rust is a fungal disease that requires both apple and cedar trees to complete its life cycle. It is caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae and is common in regions where both hosts are present.
symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on leaves
Swollen lesions on fruit
Premature leaf drop
Gelatinous spore structures on nearby cedar trees
treatment: Remove nearby cedar trees if feasible

Apple___healthy.about: The apple plant appears healthy with no visible symptoms of disease or infection. Leaves are green, intact, and functioning normally, indicating proper physiological health.
prevention: Regularly monitor for early disease signs

Blueberry___healthy.about: The blueberry plant is in a healthy state with no signs of disease. Proper soil acidity and nutrient levels contribute to optimal growth.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.about: Powdery mildew is a fungal disease that appears as a white powdery coating on plant surfaces. It thrives in warm, dry climates with high humidity.
symptoms: White powdery growth on leaves
Leaf curling and distortion
Reduced photosynthesis
Stunted plant growth
treatment: Apply sulfur or potassium bicarbonate fungicides

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.about: The cherry plant shows no visible disease symptoms and is growing under optimal conditions.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.about: Gray leaf spot is a fungal disease caused by Cercospora species. It reduces photosynthetic efficiency and can significantly affect yield.
symptoms: Rectangular gray lesions on leaves
Lesions running parallel to leaf veins
Leaf blighting in severe cases

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.about: Common rust is caused by the fungus Puccinia sorghi. It is characterized by small, reddish-brown pustules that can occur on both surfaces of the leaf.
symptoms: Circular to elongate cinnamon-brown pustules
Pustules rupture to release powdery spores
Chlorosis and death of heavily infected leaves
treatment: Apply fungicides if infection is severe early in the season
prevention: Plant early to avoid peak spore periods

Corn-Common_rust.about: Common rust is caused by the fungus Puccinia sorghi. It is characterized by small, reddish-brown pustules that can occur on both surfaces of the leaf.
symptoms: Circular to elongate cinnamon-brown pustules
Pustules rupture to release powdery spores
Chlorosis and death of heavily infected leaves
treatment: Apply fungicides if infection is severe early in the season
prevention: Plant early to avoid peak spore periods

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.about: Caused by Exserohilum turcicum, this disease can cause significant yield loss in susceptible hybrids, especially during wet seasons.
symptoms: Large, cigar-shaped, tan to gray lesions
Lesions can merge to cover large leaf areas
Premature drying of leaves
prevention: Utilization of hybrids with polygenic resistance

Corn_(maize)___healthy.about: Corn plants are robust with vibrant green leaves and no signs of lesion development or rust pustules.
prevention: Soil testing and balanced NPK application

Grape___Black_rot.about: Black rot is caused by Guignardia bidwellii. It is a highly destructive disease that can completely destroy a harvest if not controlled.
symptoms: Small brown spots on leaves with black borders
Sunken black lesions on stems
Berries turn brown and then shrivel into hard black 'mummies'
treatment: Intensive fungicide program starting at bud break
Prune and destroy all mummified berries
prevention: Maximize airflow through proper vine training
Remove wild grapes in the vicinity

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).about: Esca is a complex of diseases caused by several fungi. It affects the vascular system of the vine, often appearing in older vineyards.
symptoms: Tiger-stripe patterns of chlorosis and necrosis on leaves
Small dark spots (measles) on berry skins
Wood decay visible in trunk cross-sections
treatment: No chemical cure exists for infected vines

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.about: Caused by Pseudocercospora vitis, this disease primarily affects older leaves in late summer but can cause premature defoliation.
symptoms: Irregularly shaped dark brown spots
Spots may merge to form large necrotic patches
Premature leaf drop leading to poor berry ripening
treatment: Standard grape fungicides used for black rot/mildew often suppress leaf blight

Grape___healthy.about: Grape vines show strong vigor, uniform leaf color, and healthy berry development.
prevention: Regular pruning and dormant season sanitation

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).about: Huanglongbing (HLB) is one of the most serious citrus diseases globally, caused by the bacterium Candidatus Liberibacter and spread by the Asian citrus psyllid.
symptoms: Asymmetrical yellow mottling on leaves
Small, bitter, misshapen fruit that remains green at the bottom
Stunted growth and twig dieback
treatment: No known cure; infected trees should be removed to prevent spread
prevention: Control psyllid populations using insecticides and biological controls

Peach___Bacterial_spot.about: Caused by Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni, this disease affects leaves, fruit, and twigs of stone fruits.
symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots that turn purple or brown
Shot-hole appearance on leaves (centers of spots fall out)
Cracking and pitting of fruit surface
treatment: Oxytetracycline applications during the growing season

Peach___healthy.about: Peach tree exhibits lush foliage and smooth, unblemished fruit development.
prevention: Prune during dormancy to maintain airflow
Maintain mulch layer for moisture retention

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.about: A devastating disease for peppers in warm, humid climates, caused by species of Xanthomonas.
symptoms: Small, circular raised spots on fruit
Water-soaked lesions on the underside of leaves
Defoliation and sunscald on exposed fruit
treatment: Apply copper fungicides mixed with mancozeb
prevention: Avoid working in the field when plants are wet

Pepper,_bell___healthy.about: The bell pepper plant is healthy, featuring dark green foliage and firm, shiny fruit.
prevention: Drip irrigation to keep leaves dry

Potato___Early_blight.about: Caused by the fungus Alternaria solani. Despite the name, it can occur at any point in the growing season.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (bullseye appearance)
Yellowing of surrounding leaf tissue
Lower leaves usually affected first
treatment: Apply fungicides such as chlorothalonil or mancozeb
Ensure plants are well-fertilized to reduce stress
prevention: Crop rotation of at least 3 years
Removal of potato 'volunteers' from previous seasons

Potato-Barly blight.about: Caused by the fungus Alternaria solani. Despite the name, it can occur at any point in the growing season.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (bullseye appearance)
Yellowing of surrounding leaf tissue
Lower leaves usually affected first
treatment: Apply fungicides such as chlorothalonil or mancozeb
Ensure plants are well-fertilized to reduce stress
prevention: Crop rotation of at least 3 years
Removal of potato 'volunteers' from previous seasons

Potato___Late_blight.about: Caused by Phytophthora infestans, the pathogen responsible for the Irish Potato Famine. It spreads rapidly in cool, wet weather.
symptoms: Water-soaked dark green to black spots on leaves
White fuzzy growth on the underside of leaves in humid conditions
Rotting tubers with a reddish-brown dry rot
treatment: Aggressive fungicide application at first sign of disease

Potato___healthy.about: Potato foliage is green and vigorous, with no signs of blight or tuber rot.

Raspberry___healthy.about: Raspberry canes are strong with healthy leaves and no evidence of fungal or viral infection.
prevention: Removal of old canes after harvest

Soybean___healthy.about: Soybean plants show uniform growth and no signs of cyst nematodes or rust.
prevention: Crop rotation with corn or wheat
Soil testing for pH and nutrients

Squash___Powdery_mildew.about: A common fungal disease in cucurbits that covers leaves in a white flour-like substance.
symptoms: White, circular powdery spots on leaves and stems
Yellowing and browning of leaves
Premature leaf senescence
treatment: Fungicides containing sulfur or neem oil

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.about: Caused by the fungus Diplocarpon earlianum, it primarily affects the foliage and can weaken the plant.
symptoms: Small purplish spots that enlarge into irregular dark patches
Centers of spots remain dark (unlike leaf spot)
Leaves may dry up and look scorched
treatment: Apply fungicides after harvest and during early spring
Mow and remove foliage after harvest
prevention: Remove weeds to improve air circulation

Strawberry___healthy.about: Strawberry plants show bright green leaves and healthy runners without spotting.
prevention: Straw mulching to keep berries off the soil

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.about: A bacterial disease that affects all above-ground parts of the plant, favored by high temperature and high humidity.
symptoms: Small, water-soaked, greasy spots on leaves
Scabby, dark lesions on fruit surface
Yellowing of leaves and eventual leaf drop
treatment: Streptomycin can be used in some regions for prevention in seedlings
prevention: Rotate with non-solanaceous crops every 3 years

Tomato-Bacterial_spot.about: A bacterial disease that affects all above-ground parts of the plant, favored by high temperature and high humidity.
symptoms: Small, water-soaked, greasy spots on leaves
Scabby, dark lesions on fruit surface
Yellowing of leaves and eventual leaf drop
treatment: Streptomycin can be used in some regions for prevention in seedlings
prevention: Rotate with non-solanaceous crops every 3 years

Tomato___Early_blight.about: Caused by Alternaria solani, this is one of the most common tomato diseases, starting on the lower leaves.
symptoms: Concentric rings in dark brown leaf spots
Stem cankers near the soil line
Leathery black spots on the stem end of fruit
treatment: Prune lower leaves to prevent soil splash
prevention: Mulch around the base of plants

Tomato___Late_blight.about: A fast-moving and destructive disease caused by Phytophthora infestans.
symptoms: Large, irregular greenish-black water-soaked patches
White fungal-like growth on the undersides of leaves
Firm, dark brown decay on fruit
treatment: Destroying infected plants to prevent airborne spread
prevention: Planting resistant varieties like 'Iron Lady' or 'Defiant'

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.about: Caused by Passalora fulva, this disease is most common in greenhouse environments with high humidity.
symptoms: Pale green or yellowish spots on upper leaf surfaces
Olive-green to brown velvety mold on the underside of leaves
Leaves eventually wither and drop

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.about: A very common fungal disease that starts at the bottom of the plant and moves up.
symptoms: Small circular spots with dark borders and gray centers
Tiny black specks (fruiting bodies) in the centers of spots
Extensive defoliation starting from the base
treatment: Apply fungicides every 7–10 days in wet weather
prevention: Control solanaceous weeds around the garden
Mulching to prevent soil-borne spores from splashing

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.about: Spider mites are tiny arachnids that suck the sap from tomato leaves, especially during hot, dry weather.
symptoms: Fine yellow or white stippling (dots) on leaves
Very fine webbing on stems and under leaves
Leaves turn bronze and dry up
treatment: Apply insecticidal soap or neem oil
prevention: Mist plants with water to increase local humidity

Tomato___Target_Spot.about: Caused by the fungus Corynespora cassiicola, this disease produces spots that look like targets.
symptoms: Circular brown spots with faint concentric rings
Fruit develops small, circular, sunken lesions
Large necrotic areas on foliage

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.about: A viral disease transmitted by the silverleaf whitefly. It is one of the most damaging tomato viruses.
symptoms: Severe stunting of the plant
Leaves curl upward and become chlorotic (yellow)
Flowers often drop, resulting in no fruit production
treatment: No cure for the virus; remove and destroy infected plants
prevention: Use row covers to exclude whiteflies

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.about: A highly stable virus that can be spread by hands, tools, and some insects.
symptoms: Mottling of green and yellow on leaves
Fern-leaf appearance (narrowing of leaves)
Internal browning of the fruit
treatment: No chemical treatment; pull and burn infected plants
Wash hands and tools with soap/disinfectant after contact
prevention: Do not smoke around tomato plants (virus can be in tobacco)

Tomato___healthy.about: The tomato plant is vibrant with strong stems and healthy foliage, showing no signs of fungal spots or viral stunting.
prevention: Stake or cage plants to keep fruit off the ground
Regular pruning of suckers for airflow
